title: Local ablative treatment for oligoprogression during immunotherapy in metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Local ablative treatment for oligoprogression during immunotherapy in metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s0001-p1】Metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is not one disease state. Contemporary registries indicate that 30%–40% of newly diagnosed stage IV cases meet anatomical criteria for limited metastatic spread, 1 and, among patients progressing on anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), between 30% and 60% do so at a limited number of sites. 2 , 3 In a lung cancer cohort enriched for acquired resistance to anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy, Schoenfeld and colleagues 4 found that oligo-acquired resistance, with disease elsewhere remaining controlled, was present in 56% of patients; these patients had higher baseline tumor mutational burden and deeper, longer initial responses than patients with systemic acquired resistance. A plausible explanation is immune editing: antigen-recognizable clones are eliminated, whereas the clones that persist at focal sites have acquired immune evasion through PD-L1 heterogeneity, loss of antigen presentation, or oncogenic signaling that restores proliferative autonomy independent of checkpoint pressure. 4 , 5 Systemic benefit can persist while one or two lesions escape.

【Introduction · s0001-p2】Three related terms recur in this literature and are not interchangeable. Oligoprogression, as characterized by the ESTRO and EORTC consensus, denotes progression of a few metastases during active systemic therapy while other sites remain controlled, without a fixed numerical threshold. 6 Oligo-acquired resistance is a narrower entity, defined by Schoenfeld and colleagues as progression at three or fewer lesions after a documented complete or partial response to anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy, and is therefore a subset of oligoprogression specific to ICI therapy. 4 Focal immune escape describes the underlying biology, namely, spatially restricted loss of immune control through impaired antigen presentation or reduced HLA class I expression, and is a mechanistic explanation rather than a disease-state classification. 7 We use oligoprogression throughout as the clinical entity under study.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Local ablative treatment for oligoprogression during immunotherapy in metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · s0003-p3】Radiotherapy was the dominant modality. Of the 145 patients in the LAT arms of the five primary studies, 112 were enrolled in studies in which radiotherapy was the only permitted modality (Brown et al., Friedes et al., and CURB). Jiang et al. 30 reported the distribution for their 16 treated patients as radiotherapy in 13, surgery in 2, and another local intervention in 1. At least 125 of 145 patients (86%) therefore received radiotherapy, and surgical resection is documented in only 2. Xuzhang et al. 3 recorded LAT as a binary variable in 17 patients and did not disaggregate radiation from surgery. Modality was not used as a stratification variable. Sensitivity analyses restricted to the radiotherapy-only studies are reported below; those studies permitted both ablative and conventionally fractionated techniques, so these analyses do not isolate ablative dose. Most patients had received first-line or second-line immunotherapy, and progression was limited to 1–5 sites at the time of LAT (per-study thresholds and time zero in Table 2), with one study enrolling atypical mixed responses without a cap. Schellenberg et al. 26 (STOP) was retained as the principal negative randomized anchor (90 patients, 59 irradiated and 31 control, mostly NSCLC). Belaidi et al. 33 Kothari et al. 34 (NIVORAD), and Xu et al. 35 contributed to qualified sensitivity analyses but not the primary pool because their population definitions were broader, their comparator was a timing contrast, or the continuation strategy was less uniform.

【Results · s0003-p5】Four studies contributed to the primary PFS analysis (285 patients, 106 treated with LAT). LAT with continued immunotherapy was associated with an approximately halved hazard of progression or death, pooled HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.33–0.62; 95% prediction interval 0.28–0.74; I2 = 0%; Figure 2). Four studies contributed to the primary OS analysis (308 patients, 129 treated with LAT), pooled HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.27–0.63; 95% prediction interval 0.24–0.69; I2 = 0%; Figure 3). Neither analysis showed detectable statistical heterogeneity, and both prediction intervals lay below 1.0. Excluding the PFS2 estimate of Brown et al. gave a concordant PFS estimate (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.25–0.75; prediction interval 0.19–0.95). Restricting the PFS pool to the two studies with time zero at or after oligoprogression (Xuzhang et al. and CURB) left the point estimate unchanged (HR 0.45; 95% CI 0.17–1.19, wide because only two studies contributed). The Knapp‒Hartung small-sample correction widened the intervals relative to the standard random-effects estimator, so these are the conservative figures.

【Figure 1. · f0001】Figure 1. PRISMA 2020 study-selection flow diagram.

【Figure 2. · f0002】Figure 2. Primary forest plot for progression-free survival. Random-effects meta-analysis (REML, Knapp‒Hartung adjustment) of the primary PFS analysis. The contributing studies were Brown et al. 29 *, Tsai et al. 25 (CURB, prespecified NSCLC subgroup), Jiang et al. 30 and Xuzhang et al. 3 The overall estimate represents a pooled HR with 95% CI and 95% prediction interval. *Brown et al. reported PFS2, measured from the start of first-line immunotherapy to the second progression or death; time zero for each study is given in Table 2.

【Figure 3. · f0003】Figure 3. Primary forest plot for overall survival. Random-effects meta-analysis (REML, Knapp‒Hartung adjustment) of the primary OS analysis. The contributing studies were Tsai et al. 25 (CURB, prespecified NSCLC subgroup), Friedes et al. 32 Brown et al. 29 *, and Xuzhang et al. 3 The overall estimate represents a pooled HR with 95% CI and 95% prediction interval. In Friedes et al., the contributing OS estimate was multivariable-adjusted. *Brown et al. measured OS from the start of first-line immunotherapy.
